You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From ce4bb04cae8924792ed92f4af2793b77fc986f0e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2018 18:47:05 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] Fix a leak in socket(2) when we fail to allocate a file
 descriptor.

Got broken by "make sock_alloc_file() do sock_release() on failures" -
cleanup after sock_map_fd() failure got pulled all the way into
sock_alloc_file(), but it used to serve the case when sock_map_fd()
failed *before* getting to sock_alloc_file() as well, and that got
lost.  Trivial to fix, fortunately.

Fixes: 8e1611e23579 (make sock_alloc_file() do sock_release() on failures)
Reported-by: Dmitry Vyukov <dvyukov@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
---
 net/socket.c | 4 +++-
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/net/socket.c b/net/socket.c
index 42d8e9c9ccd5..82433a2200ec 100644
--- a/net/socket.c
+++ b/net/socket.c
@@ -432,8 +432,10 @@ static int sock_map_fd(struct socket *sock, int flags)
 {
 	struct file *newfile;
 	int fd = get_unused_fd_flags(flags);
-	if (unlikely(fd < 0))
+	if (unlikely(fd < 0)) {
+		sock_release(sock);
 		return fd;
+	}
 
 	newfile = sock_alloc_file(sock, flags, NULL);
 	if (likely(!IS_ERR(newfile))) {
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by improper handling of resource cleanup in the `sock_map_fd` function. Specifically, when the allocation of a file descriptor failed (i.e., when `get_unused_fd_flags` returned a negative value), the previously allocated socket was not released, leading to a memory leak. The issue arose after a previous change that made `sock_alloc_file` responsible for releasing the socket on failure, which caused the cleanup logic for failures occurring before reaching `sock_alloc_file` to be overlooked. The fix involved adding a call to `sock_release` to ensure that the socket is properly released in case of a failure to allocate a file descriptor.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by improper handling of resource cleanup in the `sock_map_fd` function. Specifically, when the allocation of a file descriptor failed (i.e., when `get_unused_fd_flags` returned a negative value), the previously allocated socket was not released, leading to a memory leak. The issue arose after a previous change that made `sock_alloc_file` responsible for releasing the socket on failure, which caused the cleanup logic for failures occurring before reaching `sock_alloc_file` to be overlooked. The fix involved adding a call to `sock_release` to ensure that the socket is properly released in case of a failure to allocate a file descriptor.
